## Fixes

- Key labels now render on systems without Arial, which includes most Linux installs. They used to come out blank. Labels fall back to Helvetica, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, or Noto Sans, and then to any installed font.

## Release changes

- Releases are now source only, and CI publishes them. A release is a tag and these notes, with no prebuilt binary attached. Build it with Nix or Cargo, as shown below. Releases up to v0.10.0 keep their Developer ID–signed zips.
- CI runs the tests, Clippy, and rustfmt on Linux and macOS for every push and pull request.

## Install

Releases are source only: build mx-keypad with Nix or Cargo.

### Nix flake

```nix
# Pin to a release tag (recommended); drop the ref to track the default branch.
inputs.mx-keypad.url = "github:hawkish/mx-keypad/v0.10.1";
```

Or install it into your profile:

```sh
nix profile install github:hawkish/mx-keypad/v0.10.1
```

### Cargo

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/hawkish/mx-keypad --tag v0.10.1
```

On macOS, run `mx-keypad install` afterward to restart the LaunchAgent on the new build. It signs the agent with your Apple Development identity when you have one, so macOS keeps its Accessibility permission across upgrades. See the [README](https://github.com/hawkish/mx-keypad#install-and-check-a-configuration).
